title: Officely vs Skedda: Which Hybrid Work Platform Fits Slack and Teams?
summary: Compare Officely and Skedda for capacity management, desk booking, attendance visibility, workplace controls, integrations, and reporting.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


Choosing between Officely and Skedda comes down to the workflow your workplace needs. Officely takes a collaboration-first approach, keeping hybrid scheduling and booking inside Slack or Microsoft Teams. Skedda provides a broader workplace and space-booking environment across several interfaces. For effective **Capacity Management** , consider where employees already work, how much desk-capacity visibility you need, the complexity of your offices, your policy controls, and the reporting questions your workplace team must answer.


- **Choose Officely** when employees need to book desks and coordinate office days through Slack or Teams.
- **Consider Skedda** when you need more space categories, interactive floor plans, visitor management, or granular controls. This distinction is covered in more detail in the[Officely and Skedda comparison](https://getofficely.com/blog/officely-pricing-compared-to-skedda) .
- **Review user feedback before deciding.** G2’s Officely vs. Skedda comparison provides an independent place to compare user experiences[\[1\]](https://www.g2.com/compare/officely-officely-vs-skedda) .


## What capacity management means in a hybrid office


Hybrid-office Capacity Management is the process of monitoring and controlling how many people use a workplace at a given time. It connects planned attendance with available desks, meeting rooms, parking, and other office resources.


A practical system needs to show more than total capacity. Workplace teams need visibility into planned attendance, available desks, actual attendance, booking restrictions, and the data used to review hybrid-policy adherence.


Desk booking contributes to that process, but a reservation records intent. Attendance and usage data help you assess who booked, who attended, and which areas remained underused.


### From headcount to usable workplace capacity


A workplace may have room for a certain number of people, but that headline figure does not describe usable capacity. Employees also need suitable desks, access to shared rooms, and space near the colleagues they plan to work with.


Capacity can therefore apply at several levels:


- The entire office
- An individual floor
- A team neighborhood
- Desks and flexible seating areas
- Meeting rooms
- Parking areas


These units help workplace teams avoid situations where the building has room available but the required floor, neighborhood, or resource is already full.


Officely lets an administrator set a maximum capacity for an office or for specific floors and neighborhoods. Once an area reaches its limit,[the capacity-management workflow prevents further bookings](https://getofficely.com/blog/instant-capacity-management-to-keep-office-safe-productive) .


### How attendance planning and desk booking work together


Attendance planning establishes who intends to come in and when. Desk booking connects that intention to a usable place in the office. Attendance data then helps the workplace team compare the plan with what happened.


A simple workflow might look like this:


1. **Set the limit:** The workplace team defines the maximum capacity for a floor.
2. **Open reservations:** Employees choose an office day and reserve available desks.
3. **Apply the cut-off:** The platform stops further bookings when the floor reaches its limit.
4. **Review attendance:** The team compares bookings with attendance information.
5. **Adjust operations:** The team uses the result to review space allocation, policy communication, or future availability.


This flow turns office attendance tracking into an operational process. It also gives People and Operations teams clearer information than a spreadsheet or a collection of chat messages.


## Officely vs Skedda: feature comparison for capacity management


The following table compares capabilities that affect hybrid attendance, workspace capacity, and employee adoption. The main difference is the role each platform plays: Officely centers the everyday employee experience in collaboration tools, while Skedda provides a broader booking and administration environment.


Comparison criterion Officely Skedda What it means for your team


Desk and room booking Manages desks and meeting rooms from Slack and Teams Lists desk booking and meeting-room booking Both cover core workplace reservations, but employees access them through different workflows


Office and space scheduling Lets employees manage schedules, book desks, and see who is in the office within Slack or Teams Lists office-space, lab, and parking-space booking Skedda covers more booking categories, while Officely keeps hybrid-office scheduling close to daily communication


Occupancy and headcount visibility Shows who booked, who attended, and what space is underused Occupancy Insights includes daily headcount and attendance trends Both can inform capacity decisions, with different reporting and workflow models


Attendance trends and RTO reporting Shows office-use frequency, hybrid-policy adherence, and space requirements from bookings recorded in Slack and Teams Promotes RTO reports through Occupancy Insights Workplace teams can assess attendance patterns and policy performance


Custom rules and roles — Lists custom rules and roles Skedda may fit organizations that need granular control across different users and resources


Integrations Centers the employee experience in Slack and Microsoft Teams Its official site links to integrations Review where employees complete bookings and where administrators configure the system


Employee booking workflow Centered in Slack and Teams Supports Teams and Slack alongside web, mobile, maps, and calendars Officely focuses on an embedded workflow; Skedda provides several ways to access bookings


Broader workplace-management features — Lists interactive floor plans, visitor management, and Workplace Intelligence Skedda addresses a wider set of workplace-management requirements


Best-fit use case Hybrid teams that want attendance and booking centered in Slack or Teams Organizations that need broader space management, maps, and granular controls Choose according to employee habits and operational complexity rather than feature count alone


- **Desk and room booking:** Employees are more likely to complete reservations when the booking route fits their normal workday. Check whether your team wants chat-based actions or a broader booking interface.
- **Office and space scheduling:** Consider every resource that requires a reservation. A standard hybrid office may focus on desks and rooms, while laboratories or varied parking resources create a wider scheduling requirement.
- **Occupancy and headcount visibility:** Headcount shows how many people use the workplace. Booking and attendance details help explain demand, missed reservations, and underused areas.
- **Attendance trends and RTO reporting:** Reporting should answer the questions behind your hybrid policy. That may include office-use frequency, attendance expectations, or space requirements.
- **Custom rules and roles:** Granular controls become more relevant as booking policies vary by location, resource, team, or user role. Ask who will maintain those rules after launch.
- **Integrations:** An integration can provide notifications, selected actions, or a full employee workflow. Ask vendors to demonstrate how much of the booking journey happens inside Slack or Teams.
- **Employee booking workflow:** Multiple access options can support varied workplace needs. An embedded route can reduce context switching for teams that already spend the day in collaboration tools.
- **Broader workplace-management features:** Interactive maps, visitor workflows, and workplace intelligence may matter when your requirements extend beyond hybrid attendance. A focused platform can be easier to administer when those functions are outside your scope.
- **Best-fit use case:** The better choice is the one that matches how employees book and how workplace teams control space. The[comparison of Skedda alternatives](https://getofficely.com/skedda-alternatives) provides further detail about these workflow differences.


### How to use this comparison


Start by marking each criterion as required, useful, or outside your scope. Give extra weight to the employee workflow because incomplete or inconsistent bookings weaken the data used for Capacity Management.


Then assess the administrative side. Identify the space categories you manage, the policy controls you need, and the reports your workplace team must review. A long feature list adds little value when the daily workflow does not match how your company operates.


## How the two platforms handle hybrid attendance and capacity


Officely and Skedda both support workplace booking, but they organize the experience differently. Officely puts the everyday employee journey inside collaboration tools. Skedda combines collaboration-tool support with web, mobile, maps, calendars, and broader space-management controls.


### Officely: capacity management inside Slack and Teams


Employees can book desks, see who plans to attend, and manage schedules from a Slack channel or Teams chat. This[Slack and Teams workflow](https://getofficely.com/blog/officely-vs-skedda-comparison) keeps routine office coordination in tools employees already have open.


Officely also manages meeting-room and parking reservations from Slack and Teams. That gives employees one familiar place to coordinate several parts of an office day.


Bookings recorded in those tools provide daily attendance data. Workplace teams can use[office usage analytics](https://getofficely.com/solutions/office-usage-analytics) to review office-use frequency, space requirements, and whether teams meet hybrid attendance expectations.


- **Daily experience:** Employees choose office days, reserve resources, and check who else will attend in Slack or Teams.
- **Capacity connection:** Booking records show planned demand, while attendance information helps identify actual use and underused space.
- **Policy support:** Managers can review attendance against minimum office-day requirements and manage hybrid policies more consistently.
- **Team coordination:** Neighborhoods help colleagues plan to sit near one another, making shared office days easier to organize.


This approach suits teams that want desk booking software to feel like part of their normal conversation, rather than another destination on the Monday morning checklist.


### Skedda: a broader workplace and space-booking environment


Skedda’s feature navigation covers desks, meeting rooms, office space, laboratories, and parking spaces. It also lists interactive floor plans, visitor management, custom rules and roles, and Workplace Intelligence.


Occupancy Insights includes daily headcount, attendance trends, and RTO reports. These reporting areas can support organizations that need to examine attendance across varied spaces and policies.


Skedda supports Slack and Microsoft Teams alongside dedicated web and mobile experiences. The buying question is therefore about the role of each interface, rather than whether collaboration-tool support exists.


- **Daily experience:** Employees can reach bookings through several surfaces, including collaboration tools, web, mobile, maps, and calendars.
- **Capacity connection:** Multiple space categories and interactive floor plans support more varied booking environments.
- **Administrative control:** Custom rules and roles can help teams manage detailed booking requirements.
- **Reporting scope:** Occupancy Insights addresses headcount, attendance trends, and return-to-office reporting.


The broader environment may help when facilities teams manage many resource types or need visual space selection. It also gives administrators more areas to assess during procurement and rollout.


## Which platform fits your workplace?


The right choice depends on where employees will book and how much operational complexity your workplace team manages. Company size alone does not settle that question.


Consider the number and variety of spaces, the number of office locations, and the complexity of your booking policies. You should also determine whether Slack or Teams is already the natural place for employees to coordinate office attendance.


Use these questions to guide your evaluation:


- Where will employees actually book?
- Do you need office-wide or area-level capacity limits?
- Do you need daily headcount, attendance trends, or RTO reporting?
- Do you manage resources beyond desks and rooms?
- Who needs control over rules and roles?
- How will managers review minimum office-day requirements?
- Which team owns the quality of attendance data?


### Choose Officely when collaboration-first adoption is the priority


Officely is the stronger fit when employees already work extensively in Slack or Microsoft Teams. They can manage office schedules, book desks and rooms, and see who plans to attend without moving into a separate employee workflow.


It also suits teams that need visibility into bookings, attendance, and underused space. Workplace teams can use that information to review office demand and assess hybrid-policy adherence.


Office, floor, and neighborhood limits support practical Capacity Management. These controls help prevent overbooking while keeping the reservation process simple for employees.


Officely is especially relevant when your priorities include:


- Slack desk booking or Microsoft Teams desk booking
- Hybrid team coordination
- Hot desk booking for flexible seating
- Attendance visibility for managers
- Minimum office-day tracking
- Practical office utilisation analytics
- A focused administration experience


**Planning hybrid attendance through Slack or Teams?** **[Explore Officely](https://getofficely.com/)** to see how booking and workplace coordination fit into those tools.


### Consider Skedda when workplace complexity is the priority


Skedda may fit organizations that need several types of bookable space, interactive floor plans, visitor management, or detailed custom rules and roles. These requirements often arise when workplace operations extend beyond standard desk and meeting-room scheduling.


Its multi-surface environment can also suit teams that want employees and administrators to work across web, mobile, collaboration tools, maps, and calendars. During evaluation, ask which tasks each interface supports and how data moves between them.


Consider Skedda when your requirements include:


- Visual selection through interactive floor plans
- Laboratory or varied office-space booking
- Visitor-management workflows
- Granular booking rules and user roles
- A broader workplace-management setup
- Occupancy Insights for headcount, trends, and RTO reports


## Implementation considerations before you choose


A useful evaluation follows the real booking journey from the employee’s decision to attend through the workplace team’s reporting review. This exposes unnecessary steps, unclear ownership, and gaps in the data before they become rollout problems.


### Map the employee booking journey


Document how an employee currently completes each part of an office visit:


1. Decides to work from the office
2. Checks who else plans to attend
3. Reviews available capacity
4. Books a desk, room, or other resource
5. Receives reminders or updates
6. Arrives at the workplace
7. Contributes to the attendance record
8. Changes or cancels a reservation when plans shift


Ask each vendor to show this complete journey. An attractive booking screen tells you little if employees must switch tools repeatedly or managers cannot interpret the resulting records.


The desired journey will help you choose between a collaboration-first approach and a multi-surface environment. It also gives IT teams a clear picture of where access, permissions, and support responsibilities sit.


### Set capacity rules and reporting ownership


List every capacity unit your team needs to manage. Include the office, floor, neighborhood, desk, meeting room, and parking area where relevant.


Then define the required control for each unit. Officely administrators can set maximum capacity for an entire office or selected floors and neighborhoods. Further bookings stop when the relevant limit is reached.


Assign named owners for:


- Booking policies
- Office and area limits
- User access and roles
- Attendance-data review
- Hybrid-policy reporting
- Changes to space configuration


Decide which operational questions the data must answer before configuring reports. These questions may cover planned attendance, actual attendance, underused areas, and adherence to hybrid-work policies.


Officely’s Slack and Teams booking data can support daily attendance analysis. Skedda presents daily headcount, attendance trends, and RTO reports through Occupancy Insights. Ask each vendor to demonstrate the route from an employee action to an administrator’s report.


### Run a focused rollout


Choose a rollout group that represents the workflow you plan to support. Include employees who book regularly, managers who review attendance, and administrators who maintain capacity rules.


Test real workplace scenarios rather than an idealized reservation. Employees should try booking, changing plans, encountering a full area, locating colleagues, and reserving other resources they use.


During the rollout:


- Check whether employees know where to start a booking.
- Confirm that capacity limits behave as intended.
- Review whether cancellations and changes remain visible.
- Verify that managers can answer agreed reporting questions.
- Gather feedback about confusing or unnecessary steps.
- Record any manual work required from workplace administrators.


Use the findings to revise policies, ownership, and employee guidance. The goal is to confirm that the workflow produces usable data without turning desk booking into a minor administrative hobby.


## Frequently asked questions


### What should a capacity-management pilot measure before a wider rollout?


Define success measures before launch, including completed bookings, attempts made when capacity is full, attendance-data completeness, and employee feedback. Also track the support questions raised during the pilot, since repeated questions can reveal unclear labels, permissions, or policy guidance.


### What should a workplace team ask to see in a capacity-management product demo?


Ask the vendor to demonstrate the complete employee-to-admin flow using your office structure, collaboration tools, booking policies, and reporting questions. Include a changed reservation or full-capacity scenario so you can see how the system handles common exceptions.


## Make the capacity-management decision around the workflow your team will use


Effective Capacity Management depends on usable attendance, booking, and space data. A list of desks cannot show whether employees attended, whether teams coordinated their office days, or whether workplace policies work as intended.


Officely fits hybrid teams that want scheduling and booking centered in Slack or Microsoft Teams. Skedda may fit organizations that need a broader space-management environment with maps, varied resource categories, and granular controls.


Match the platform to your employees’ work habits, your space complexity, and the questions your reporting must answer. If desk booking and hybrid-office coordination belong in Slack or Teams, explore how Officely can support that workflow.
